This result pointed out that the method proposed in this research could significantly improve the accuracy of low-cost GPS receivers for automated drone applications.

articleTitle: Firefighting Robot Based On IoT and Ban Levels Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) technology is known as a system where various sensors are connected to the Internet for various real-world applications. This paper presents a prototype fire fighting robot system. The system is designed and developed by implementing IoT and ban-level techniques for monitoring and control. The robot aims to eliminate human involvement and deliver an effective firefighting system. Arduino UNO V3 is used as a microcontroller, connected to a wireless mobile application, enabling the implementation of remote control. The robot is designed in such a way that inputs taken from the infrared flame sensor, water level sensor, and smoke level detector are used to determine the movement of the water spray nozzle so that it will be directed to the fire source precisely. A prototype was successfully designed and the functionality of the system was tested. The results show that the IoT infrastructure can successfully track and control the movement of the robot and the spray direction of the nozzle.

articleTitle: The Covid-19 Total Lockdown Effects on Grid Energy Demand: A Malaysia Experience
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: The Covid-19 disease is a highly contagious disease that causes respiratory tracts and lung infections, where some of the cases can lead to fatalities. Malaysia recorded the first Covid-19 case on January 25th, 2020. Although the government at the time considered the disease was not a threat, as the days went by the cases started to increase. The total lockdown measure, also known as the movement control order (MCO) was declared by the new Government of Malaysia following the surge of Covid-19 cases in early March 2020. The new prime minister, following a change of government, announced that schools were to be closed, offices and non-essential business activities were told to cease operation, and people were ordered to stay in their homes. As a newly industrialized country, with little economic activities, there were significant drops in the energy demand in Malaysia. This paper analyzes the change in the power demand and energy consumption trend in Malaysia before, during and after the Covid-19 total lockdown.

articleTitle: Effects of Ruqyah Recitation During Phasmophobia (Fear of Ghosts) Attacks: An EEG Analytical Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of changes in electroencephalographic (EEG) signals when Ruqyah recitations are recited during the Phasmophobia attack. Phasmophobia is defined as an extreme fear of ghosts. Ruqyah recitations are used to minimize this feeling of fear. The experiment was conducted on 15 UniKL MITEC students, aged between 20-30 years. Whilst, 19 channels of CONTEC Medical EEG System KT88-3200 have been used as the main recording devices. Based on our study, there is evidence of a correlation between the psychological state, behavior and physiological signals of Phasmophobia candidates. The EEG recording generates a different type of signature regarding the level of fear the candidates encountered. Moreover, the recitation of Ruqyah can reduce the Phasmophobia episodes and transit the candidates into calm and relaxing conditions. This will lead to an advanced method for detecting Phasmophobia episodes automatically based on EEG recognition. A more physiological signal needs to be monitored and correlated with the EEG, such as the Electrocardiogram (ECG) and Electromyogram (EMG).

articleTitle: Nondestructive Testing and Evaluation of Smart Textile Sensors using Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: The integration and coating with conductive elements allows the use of textiles as flexible sensors for physical and chemical quantities. These conductive textiles combine the mechanical properties of the carrier material with the electrical characteristics of the conductive elements. Due to inhomogeneities in manufacturing as well as the influence of ageing factors, such as mechanical or chemical stress, the accuracy of these sensor systems suffers over the product lifespan. In this paper, we present a comprehensive evaluation system to detect these inhomogeneities in the textile material and measure the influence of the most common ageing factors. We compare several measuring methods from electrical engineering, medicine and chemistry in order to select the best methods for wear detection in conductive textiles. Using test stands for accelerated ageing, the ability to measure these effects was also successfully demonstrated on embedded systems. This means that the next generation of smart textile sensors systems are able to compensate for inhomogeneities in the production process as well as wear and tear due to ageing by itself. Thus, a reduction of waste, a longer lifetime of the sensor systems as well as improved accuracy can be achieved.

articleTitle: Automatic Watering System for Smart Agriculture using ESP32 Platform
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: Agriculture can be transformed into smart agriculture due to the advanced wireless network and the Internet of Things (IoT). As the human population increases, so does the demand for crops. With real-time monitoring, a smart agriculture system’s awareness of soil moisture measurement, humidity, and environmental temperature will increase food security. In addition, smart agriculture can increase crop yield, reduce water waste, and boost productivity. In light of this, this study proposes smart agriculture, which employs sensor-based monitoring in real-time without human intervention. Users have direct access to real-time data, and all sensor data is recorded and monitored at all times and from anywhere within the internet’s coverage area. The development of a mobile application facilitates growth monitoring and user access to data. This research measures yield-affecting agricultural factors such as soil moisture, humidity, and temperature. Nonetheless, monitoring environmental factors is crucial to increasing crop yields. The experiment was conducted on two chili plants, one with an automation system and one without, which were manually watered once daily at 7:00 a.m. It is estimated that the plant with the system can maintain the optimal moisture level, whereas the other plant’s moisture measurement continues to decrease. Compared to manual watering, automatic watering also results in accelerated plant growth. Consequently, a smart agriculture system is anticipated to improve plant growth and system efficiency.

articleTitle: Authentication of IoT in Smart City Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: The advancement of technology brings an extensive use of Internet of things (IoT) devices in our daily life. IoT primary used for data collection and provide real-time management information in the network paradigms such as Edge Computing and Fog Computing. However, assuring the reliability of data delivered via Edge Computing is a challenging task. Blockchain has been a technology that has gained traction in recent years. Using Blockchain with IoT allows Smart Cities (SC) applications to spread security information, which protects against Distributed Denial of Service (DDOS) attacks. IoT devices in a SC can have a lengthy life, increasing the possibility of security flaws caused by obsolete firmware. This paper will highlight the significance of the implementation considering the SC and demonstrate a testbed made up of Blockchain Ethereum and actual IoT devices. The effects of transmission time, memory, and CPU use on the sending also processing of these messages were demonstrated. The proposed Application Programming Interface (API) sign, identify, and validate the messages before collecting them for an IoT data management application.

articleTitle: Development of Self Sustainable IOT Based Low Cost UV Index Monitoring Station
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: Ultraviolet exists in our daily life as Sun is the major source of ultraviolet. Although ultraviolet is undetectable with bare eyes, but it does bring effect to our health and product lifetime under long exposure of strong ultraviolet radiation. This paper presented the development of ultraviolet index monitoring station which consisted of a low cost analogue breakout module integrated with an ultraviolet sensor, GUVA-S12SD, a wireless fidelity embedded microcontroller, NodeMCU-ESP8266, solar photovoltaic system for self sustainability of the station and a large display made of two seven segment light-emitting diode. The ultraviolet index monitoring station was connected to the internet and the ultraviolet data were sent to an Internet of Things platform, ThingSpeak for public access. The ultraviolet index monitoring station was setup and tested at a residential area. The ultraviolet data collected were analysed and validated using external reference source from the Meteorological Department, Malaysia which located at a radius distance of 6 km from the data collection site. Lastly, a fitting equation was derived to determine the ultraviolet index value. The ultraviolet results showed a promising accuracy with a low mean error of 1.31 and which close to the reference ultraviolet index provided by Meteorological Department, Malaysia. Furthermore, this paper performed study to the ultraviolet sensor breakout module which contributed to development of the ultraviolet measuring instrument. The ultraviolet index monitoring system also contributes to monitor ultraviolet index in a local area such as community park, beach, field and school to raise the public awareness.

articleTitle: Broadband Calibration of Input Impedance for Coaxial Tips Based on RF I-V, and Related Application to Dielectric Evaluation for Liquids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: This study was conducted to evaluate calibration of input impedance for coaxial tips based on RF I-V and related application to dielectric evaluation of liquids. Verification work indicated that RF I-V calibration theory for the reference plane produces results similar to those of VNA (vector network analyzer) calibration theory. The jig structure, S11 calibration and dielectric evaluation with the VNA previously proposed by the authors were applied to impedance calibration and dielectric evaluation of liquids with an RF LCR meter. Specifically, input impedance at the jig tip of a coaxial-feed-type cut-off circular waveguide was calibrated using short/open conditions and a known material (referred to here as SOM) in the frequency range of 0.10 - 3.0 GHz, and input impedance values from each termination condition after calibration were compared with theoretical values calculated via electromagnetic (EM) analysis from the analytical model upon calibration. Complex permittivity was also estimated as an inverse problem with calculated values based on EM analysis from measured values of input impedance with various liquids in the jig after calibration. The estimation results were compared with those from VNA-based S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> evaluation at frequencies of 0.50, 1.5 and 3.0 GHz, with results indicating the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Development of a IoT Based Low Cost Wearable Smart Health Monitoring System for Elderly
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: With the advancement of technology, Internet of Things was applied in many different sectors included healthcare sector. This paper presented the development of a smart health monitoring system including a wearable device and a mobile application, MyHealth. The wearable device consisted of a low-cost integrated pulse and oxygen saturation sensor (MAX30102), a temperature sensor (LM35), a Bluetooth-embedded microcontroller (NodeMCU-ESP32-Dev-Kit) and other components to solve the problem of insufficient healthcare resources for the elderly. The developed wearable device was able to connect to the MyHealth application via Bluetooth Low Energy to measure and monitor the pulse rate, oxygen saturation and body temperature. The application will notify the concerned one if the parameters go abnormal and allows authorised people to access to the health parameter from the application. Besides, this paper discussed the calibration of the system with commercial medical devices as reference. The health monitoring system was tested by the several peoples including an elder and was able to provide pulse rate with a promising accuracy of 6 beats-per-minutes, oxygen saturation with an accuracy of 1% and body temperature with an accuracy of 1.3°Celsius when compared to the commercial products with a higher price range. This paper showed the potential of implement Internet of Things in healthcare sector with low cost. It can promote the usage of Internet of Things in community and improve the quality of life of elderly. Furthermore, this system can raise the public awareness to pay more attention to the health condition and needs of the elderly.

articleTitle: Pattern-Driven 4D Printed PLA Actuators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) printing is a technology that allows fabricating complex structures that have the ability to change their shape based on various stimuli. Such structures are printed using smart materials, which mainly rely on shape memory polymers. Controlling the response of 4D printed structures becomes challenging when increasing the complexity of the design. This paper investigates the effect of the printing patterns on the deformation performance of polylactic acid (PLA) actuators. The actuators are printed using the fused deposition modelling method. Four different patterns, namely, rectilinear, grid, honeycomb, and triangular patterns are used to develop eight actuators’ designs. The size of the patterns was varied in order to print the actuators using different infill percentages. The PLA actuators are activated using hot water of 85°C. The results show that the bending angle of the actuators is varied between 3.00° and 16.80°. The bending direction is affected by the size of the printing pattern, where the actuators bend towards the pattern with the bigger size. The results show that the proposed concept can be used in various pattern-based 4D printed robotics applications, where the actuation performance is tuned using the printing patterns, as well as the printing parameters.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Coplanar ECT
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: In this work, an Electrical Capacitance Tomography (ECT) coplanar sensor design is used to detect the presence of oil beneath ice, alongside estimating its depth and thickness. Oil spill response in the arctic region requires a non-intrusive and efficient method to detect and measure oil under ice, and this is where the role of coplanar ECT comes in. Traditional methods of solving the inverse problem in ECT are limited when it comes to coplanar sensors, as most previous works tackle ECT with a circular architecture. In this paper, we explore the use of Machine Learning techniques to detect and estimate oil under ice. The analysis of our models shows that Support Vector Machine performs best for oil detection, with a detection accuracy higher than 90%. For oil thickness and depth estimation, Random Forest performs best with a mean absolute error of 0.82mm for thickness and 1.65mm for depth. The addition of Gaussian noise to the detection and estimation datasets demonstrates our models’ robustness.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization Based on BLE Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: Radio frequency-based indoor localization system has attracted commercial developers and researchers in the last few decades. This paper presents an indoor localization system using a wireless sensor network (WSN) with a simple configuration, algorithm, and easy deployment, expansion, and improvement. Sensor nodes use Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) technology and operate at the band of 2.4 GHz. Our proposed system used 3 beacons with a grid resolution of $1m\times1m$, which applied the fingerprint method with existed advertising channel of Bluetooth Low Energy, 30 reference points, and 18 test points. The mean error of 1.0672 m in a very complex indoor environment of $9.2 m\times8.4m$ area, is a good result compared to other related works. The indoor localization system can greatly increase its accuracy by increasing the number of reference points.

articleTitle: Optimized PID Controller for Upgraded Water Distribution System Utilizing Swarm Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: In this study, the implementation of an off-line optimization for PID controller using two swarm intelligence algorithms with MATLAB and Simulink Tools simulation for the laboratory-scaled upgraded water distribution system (UWDS), is executed. Using a newly developed transfer function for the automated water level controller in the UWDS, a PID controller applied to the system is optimized using the Particle Swarm optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf optimization (GWO) technique to increase the performance of the controller. The obtained optimum result from the optimization allows more efficient and higher stability of the system which gives better automated control during the transfer of water from the supply tank to the reservoir tank. The optimization is compared between the previous water distribution system (WDS) and UWDS while analyzing the performance of both optimization techniques on the PID controller, PID-PSO, and PID-GWO. From the results obtained, the second order transfer function yields the best results when applied with both PSO and GWO optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptive Threshold Clustering in Abnormal Cardiac Beat Detection on Lightweight Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 8th International Conference on Smart Instrumentation, Measurement and Applications (ICSIMA)
abstract: Clustering is an important aspect of data mining and understanding signals. Reducing cost and processing time with high accuracy in cardiac disorder diagnosis based on clustering algorithms in electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is a critical research area. Currently, an automatic QRS complex clustering algorithm with high speed and accuracy is a challenge because of the morphological and temporal features of the ECG signals under different physical circumstances. This paper proposes a new beat clustering algorithm for ECG signals to handle these issues. Our approach utilizes the Pearson similarity and coefficient of variation that measures the dispersion of data. The strong point of our proposal employs a self-adaptive threshold for learning and detection instead of a manual threshold. We use the MIT-BIH database for testing and comparing the results. When automatically clustering, Se, Sp, and Ac values are higher than 1.52%, 7.36%, and 1.7%, respectively, compared to the previous study. We get 99.33% for specific and 99.75% for accuracy with the manual setup. Processing time for clustering is reduced by $7\times$ and keeps the same time for the abnormal beat detection stage compared with the previous research. Therefore, the suggestion is efficient for real-time clustering and abnormal beat detection on embedded devices.
